tagline: Out of the Silver Queen and up past timberline.
intro: Georgetown sits at 8,530 feet near the head of the Clear Creek valley. Guanella Pass Road leaves it southward and climbs eleven miles to the pass, then runs down Geneva Creek to Grant. Going up, it passes through spruce, fir, aspen and pine along cascading creeks, then into broad meadows where beavers work the streams, and crests well above timberline on tundra.

The road crosses the divide between the Clear Creek and South Platte watersheds. The pass was named in 1953 for Byron Guanella, a Clear Creek County road supervisor and commissioner for nearly fifty years.

moments.title: Georgetown
moments.text: The Silver Queen of Colorado in the silver boom, a town hemmed in along Clear Creek with its historic downtown at the upper, southern end.

moments.title: Guanella Pass
moments.text: At 11,669 feet a trail leaves the summit for Mount Bierstadt, named for the landscape painter who made its first recorded climb in 1863.

moments.title: Grant
moments.text: The road comes out at a retired general store and a post office at the mouth of Geneva Creek, on the North Fork of the South Platte.

practical: Paved end to end. In winter it closes, from about late November until Memorial Day weekend, at Naylor Lake on the Georgetown side and Burning Bear Campground on the Grant side.

sources.label: Colorado Department of Transportation, Guanella Pass
